١٥٤٢ — عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى؛ فَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى اللهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فَهِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى اللهِ وَرَسُولِهِ، وَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ لِدُنْيَا يُصِيبُهَا، أَوِ امْرَأَةٍ يَتَزَوَّجُهَا، فَهِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى مَا هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهِ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١)، ومسلم (١٩٠٧).

english_source:
1542 — ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Actions are only by intentions, and every person will have only what he intended. Whoever’s migration was to Allah and His Messenger, then his migration was to Allah and His Messenger. And whoever’s migration was for some worldly gain he wished to obtain, or for a woman he wished to marry, then his migration was for that to which he migrated.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1) and Muslim (1907).

١٥٤٣ — عن أنس قال: طلب بعض أصحاب النبي ﷺ وضوءًا، فقال رسول الله ﷺ:
«هَلْ مَعَ أَحَدٍ مِنْكُمْ مَاءٌ؟»
فوضع يده في الماء وهو يقول:
«تَوَضَّئُوا بِسْمِ اللهِ».
فرأيت الماء يخرج من بين أصابعه حتى توضؤوا من عند آخرهم.
قال ثابت: قلت لأنس: كم تراهم؟
قال: نحوًا من سبعين.
صحيح: رواه النسائي (٧٨)، وأحمد (١٢٦٩٤)، وصححه ابن خزيمة (١٤٤).

english_source:
1543 — Anas said: Some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ sought water for wuḍūʾ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“Does any one of you have water?”
He placed his hand into the water and said:
“Perform wuḍūʾ in the name of Allah.”
I saw water flowing from between his fingers until every one of them, down to the last person, had performed wuḍūʾ.
Thābit said: I asked Anas: “Approximately how many were they?”
He replied: “About seventy.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (78) and Aḥmad (12694); authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (144).

١٥٤٤ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
«لَا تُقْبَلُ صَلَاةُ أَحَدِكُمْ إِذَا أَحْدَثَ حَتَّى يَتَوَضَّأَ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٣٥)، ومسلم (٢٢٥).
وفي رواية عند البخاري: فقال رجل من حضرموت: ما الحدث يا أبا هريرة؟
قال: فُساء أو ضُراط.

english_source:
1544 — Abū Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“The prayer of one of you is not accepted after he breaks his state of purification until he performs wuḍūʾ.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (135) and Muslim (225).
In another narration of al-Bukhārī, a man from Ḥaḍramawt asked:
“What is ḥadath, O Abū Hurayrah?”
He replied:
“Passing wind, whether silently or audibly.”

١٥٤٥ — عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«لَا يَقْبَلُ اللهُ صَلَاةً بِغَيْرِ طُهُورٍ، وَلَا صَدَقَةً مِنْ غُلُولٍ».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٢٤).
arabic_display:
١٥٤٥ — عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«لَا يَقْبَلُ اللهُ صَلَاةً بِغَيْرِ طُهُورٍ، وَلَا صَدَقَةً مِنْ غُلُولٍ».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٢٤).
english_source:
1545 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Allah does not accept prayer without purification, nor charity from ghulūl.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (224).
Ghulūl means unlawfully taking from the spoils of war before their proper distribution.

١٥٤٦ — عن ابن عباس قال: كنا عند رسول الله ﷺ، فأتى الخلاء، ثم إنه رجع فأُتي بطعام، فقلنا: يا رسول الله، ألا نتوضأ؟
فقال:
«أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُصَلِّيَ فَأَتَوَضَّأَ؟»
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٣٧٤).
ورواه أبو داود (٣٧٦٠)، والترمذي (١٨٤٧)، والنسائي (١٣٢) بلفظ:
«إِنَّمَا أُمِرْتُ بِالْوُضُوءِ إِذَا قُمْتُ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ».
وصححه ابن خزيمة (٣٥)، وقال الترمذي: حسن.

english_source:
1546 — Ibn ʿAbbās said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he went to relieve himself. He then returned and food was brought to him.
We said:
“O Messenger of Allah, should we not bring you water for wuḍūʾ?”
He replied:
“Do I intend to pray, so that I should perform wuḍūʾ?”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (374).
Abū Dāwūd (3760), al-Tirmidhī (1847), and al-Nasāʾī (132) narrate the wording:
“I was only commanded to perform wuḍūʾ when I rise for prayer.”
Ibn Khuzaymah authenticated it (35), and al-Tirmidhī graded it Ḥasan.

١٥٤٦ — عن ابن عباس قال: كنا عند رسول الله ﷺ، فأتى الخلاء، ثم إنه رجع فأُتي بطعام، فقلنا: يا رسول الله، ألا نتوضأ؟
فقال:
«أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُصَلِّيَ فَأَتَوَضَّأَ؟»
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٣٧٤).
ورواه أبو داود (٣٧٦٠)، والترمذي (١٨٤٧)، والنسائي (١٣٢) بلفظ:
«إِنَّمَا أُمِرْتُ بِالْوُضُوءِ إِذَا قُمْتُ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ».
وصححه ابن خزيمة (٣٥)، وقال الترمذي: حسن.
1546 — Ibn ʿAbbās said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he went to relieve himself. He then returned and food was brought to him.
We said:
“O Messenger of Allah, should we not bring you water for wuḍūʾ?”
He replied:
“Do I intend to pray, so that I should perform wuḍūʾ?”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (374).

“I was only commanded to perform wuḍūʾ when I rise for prayer.”
Ibn Khuzaymah authenticated it (35), and al-Tirmidhī graded it Ḥasan.

«مِفْتَاحُ الصَّلَاةِ الطُّهُورُ، وَتَحْرِيمُهَا التَّكْبِيرُ، وَتَحْلِيلُهَا التَّسْلِيمُ».

“The key to prayer is purification; its commencement that makes ordinary actions prohibited is the takbīr, and its conclusion that makes them permissible again is the taslīm.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (61), al-Tirmidhī (3), and Ibn Mājah (275).

١٥٥١ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«إِذَا تَوَضَّأَ الْعَبْدُ الْمُسْلِمُ فَغَسَلَ وَجْهَهُ خَرَجَ مِنْ وَجْهِهِ كُلُّ خَطِيئَةٍ نَظَرَ إِلَيْهَا بِعَيْنَيْهِ مَعَ الْمَاءِ — أَوْ مَعَ آخِرِ قَطْرِ الْمَاءِ — فَإِذَا غَسَلَ يَدَيْهِ خَرَجَ مِنْ يَدَيْهِ كُلُّ خَطِيئَةٍ بَطَشَتْهَا يَدَاهُ مَعَ الْمَاءِ — أَوْ مَعَ آخِرِ قَطْرِ الْمَاءِ — فَإِذَا غَسَلَ رِجْلَيْهِ خَرَجَتْ كُلُّ خَطِيئَةٍ مَشَتْهَا رِجْلَاهُ مَعَ الْمَاءِ — أَوْ مَعَ آخِرِ قَطْرِ الْمَاءِ — حَتَّى يَخْرُجَ نَقِيًّا مِنَ الذُّنُوبِ».
صحيح: رواه مالك (٣١)، ومسلم (٢٤٤).

english_source:
1551 — Abū Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When the Muslim servant performs wuḍūʾ and washes his face, every sin at which his eyes looked leaves his face with the water—or with the last drop of the water.
When he washes his hands, every sin committed by his hands leaves his hands with the water—or with the last drop of the water.
When he washes his feet, every sin toward which his feet walked leaves with the water—or with the last drop of the water—until he emerges purified from sins.”
Authentic: Narrated by Mālik (31) and Muslim (244).

١٥٥٢ — عن عثمان بن عفان قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«مَنْ تَوَضَّأَ فَأَحْسَنَ الْوُضُوءَ خَرَجَتْ خَطَايَاهُ مِنْ جَسَدِهِ، حَتَّى تَخْرُجَ مِنْ تَحْتِ أَظْفَارِهِ».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤٥).

1552 — ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever performs wuḍūʾ and perfects his wuḍūʾ, his sins leave his body until they even emerge from beneath his fingernails.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (245).

arabic_source:
١٥٥٣ — عن حُمران مولى عثمان قال: أتيت عثمان بن عفان بوضوء، فتوضأ، ثم قال: إن ناسًا يحدثون عن رسول الله ﷺ أحاديث لا أدري ما هي، إلا أني رأيت رسول الله ﷺ توضأ مثل وضوئي هذا، ثم قال:
«مَنْ تَوَضَّأَ هَكَذَا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ، وَكَانَتْ صَلَاتُهُ وَمَشْيُهُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ نَافِلَةً».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٢٩).

english_source:
1553 — Ḥumrān, the freed servant of ʿUthmān, said: I brought ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān water for wuḍūʾ, and he performed wuḍūʾ. He then said: Some people narrate reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that I do not know, but I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform wuḍūʾ in the same manner as this wuḍūʾ of mine, and then he said:
“Whoever performs wuḍūʾ in this manner will have his previous sins forgiven, while his prayer and his walking to the mosque will be additional voluntary deeds for him.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (229).

arabic_source:
١٥٥٤ — عن إسحاق بن سعيد بن عمرو بن سعيد بن العاص قال: حدثني أبي، عن أبيه قال: كنت عند عثمان بن عفان، فدعا بطَهور، فقال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«مَا مِنِ امْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ تَحْضُرُهُ صَلَاةٌ مَكْتُوبَةٌ، فَيُحْسِنُ وُضُوءَهَا وَخُشُوعَهَا وَرُكُوعَهَا، إِلَّا كَانَتْ كَفَّارَةً لِمَا قَبْلَهَا مِنَ الذُّنُوبِ، مَا لَمْ يُؤْتِ كَبِيرَةً، وَذَلِكَ الدَّهْرَ كُلَّهُ».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٢٨).

english_source:
1554 — Isḥāq ibn Saʿīd ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: My father narrated to me from his father, who said: I was with ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān when he called for water for purification and said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“No Muslim man is present when an obligatory prayer becomes due and then performs its wuḍūʾ properly, perfects its humility and its bowing, except that it becomes an expiation for the sins that preceded it, so long as he does not commit a major sin; and this applies for all time.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (228).

arabic_source:
١٥٥٥ — عن حُمران بن أبان قال: كنت أضع لعثمان طَهورَه، فما أتى عليه يوم إلا وهو يفيض عليه نُطفةً. وقال عثمان: حدثنا رسول الله ﷺ عند انصرافنا من صلاتنا هذه — قال مِسعر: أراها العصر — فقال:
«لَا أَدْرِي أُحَدِّثُكُمْ بِشَيْءٍ أَوْ أَسْكُتُ».
فقلنا: يا رسول الله، إن كان خيرًا فحدثنا، وإن كان غير ذلك فالله ورسوله أعلم.
قال:
«مَا مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ يَتَطَهَّرُ فَيُتِمُّ الطُّهُورَ الَّذِي كَتَبَ اللهُ عَلَيْهِ، فَيُصَلِّي هَذِهِ الصَّلَوَاتِ الْخَمْسَ، إِلَّا كَانَتْ كَفَّارَاتٍ لِمَا بَيْنَهُنَّ».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٣١).

english_source:
1555 — Ḥumrān ibn Abān said: I used to prepare ʿUthmān’s water for purification, and hardly a day passed without him pouring some water over himself.
ʿUthmān said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke to us as we were leaving this prayer—Misʿar said: I think it was the ʿAṣr prayer—and said:
“I do not know whether I should tell you something or remain silent.”
We said:
“O Messenger of Allah, if it is something good, then tell us; and if it is otherwise, then Allah and His Messenger know best.”
He said:
“No Muslim purifies himself and completes the purification that Allah has prescribed for him, and then performs these five prayers, except that they become expiations for what occurs between them.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (231).

١٥٥٦ — عن حُمران مولى عثمان قال: توضأ عثمان يومًا وضوءًا حسنًا، ثم قال: رأيت رسول الله ﷺ توضأ فأحسن الوضوء، ثم قال:
«مَنْ تَوَضَّأَ هَكَذَا، ثُمَّ خَرَجَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ لَا يَنْهَزُهُ إِلَّا الصَّلَاةُ، غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا خَلَا مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٣٢).
وقوله: «ما خلا من ذنبه»؛ أي: ما مضى من ذنبه.

english_source:
1556 — Ḥumrān, the freed servant of ʿUthmān, said: One day ʿUthmān performed wuḍūʾ and performed it well. He then said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform wuḍūʾ and perfect it, and then he said:
“Whoever performs wuḍūʾ like this and then goes out to the mosque, with nothing driving him except the prayer, will have what has passed of his sins forgiven.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (232).
The expression “what has passed of his sins” means his preceding sins.

١٥٥٧ — عن أبي مالك الأشعري قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الْإِيمَانِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلَأُ الْمِيزَانَ، وَسُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلَآنِ — أَوْ تَمْلَأُ — مَا بَيْنَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ، وَالصَّدَقَةُ بُرْهَانٌ، وَالصَّبْرُ ضِيَاءٌ، وَالْقُرْآنُ حُجَّةٌ لَكَ أَوْ عَلَيْكَ، كُلُّ النَّاسِ يَغْدُو، فَبَائِعٌ نَفْسَهُ فَمُعْتِقُهَا أَوْ مُوبِقُهَا».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٢٣).

1557 — Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Purification is half of faith. ‘All praise belongs to Allah’ fills the Scale. ‘Glory be to Allah’ and ‘all praise belongs to Allah’ fill—or fills—what is between the heavens and the earth. Prayer is light, charity is proof, patience is illumination, and the Qurʾān is evidence either for you or against you. Every person goes out in the morning and sells his soul, either setting it free or destroying it.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (223).

arabic_source:
١٥٥٨ — عن أبي أمامة قال: قال عمرو بن عبسة السلمي: كنت وأنا في الجاهلية أظن أن الناس على ضلالة، وأنهم ليسوا على شيء وهم يعبدون الأوثان، فسمعت برجل بمكة يخبر أخبارًا، فقعدت على راحلتي، فقدمت عليه، فإذا رسول الله ﷺ مستخفٍ، جُرَآءُ عليه قومه، فتلطفت حتى دخلت عليه بمكة، فقلت له: ما أنت؟
قال:
«أَنَا نَبِيٌّ».
فقلت: وما نبي؟
قال:
«أَرْسَلَنِي اللهُ».
فقلت: وبأي شيء أرسلك؟
قال:
«أَرْسَلَنِي بِصِلَةِ الْأَرْحَامِ، وَكَسْرِ الْأَوْثَانِ، وَأَنْ يُوَحَّدَ اللهُ لَا يُشْرَكُ بِهِ شَيْءٌ».
قلت: فمن معك على هذا؟
قال:
«حُرٌّ وَعَبْدٌ».
قال: ومعه يومئذ أبو بكر وبلال ممن آمن به.
فقلت: إني متبعك.
قال:
«إِنَّكَ لَا تَسْتَطِيعُ ذَلِكَ يَوْمَكَ هَذَا، أَلَا تَرَى حَالِي وَحَالَ النَّاسِ؟ وَلَكِنِ ارْجِعْ إِلَى أَهْلِكَ، فَإِذَا سَمِعْتَ بِي قَدْ ظَهَرْتُ فَأْتِنِي».
قال: فذهبت إلى أهلي، وقدم رسول الله ﷺ المدينة، وكنت في أهلي، فجعلت أتخبر الأخبار وأسأل الناس حين قدم المدينة، حتى قدم علي نفر من أهل يثرب — من أهل المدينة — فقلت: ما فعل هذا الرجل الذي قدم المدينة؟
فقالوا: الناس إليه سراع، وقد أراد قومه قتله فلم يستطيعوا ذلك.
فقدمت المدينة، فدخلت عليه، فقلت: يا رسول الله، أتعرفني؟
قال:
«نَعَمْ، أَنْتَ الَّذِي لَقِيتَنِي بِمَكَّةَ».
فقلت: بلى.
فقلت: يا نبي الله، أخبرني عما علمك الله وأجهله، أخبرني عن الصلاة.
قال:
«صَلِّ صَلَاةَ الصُّبْحِ، ثُمَّ أَقْصِرْ عَنِ الصَّلَاةِ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ حَتَّى تَرْتَفِعَ؛ فَإِنَّهَا تَطْلُعُ حِينَ تَطْلُعُ بَيْنَ قَرْنَيْ شَيْطَانٍ، وَحِينَئِذٍ يَسْجُدُ لَهَا الْكُفَّارُ. ثُمَّ صَلِّ؛ فَإِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ مَشْهُودَةٌ مَحْضُورَةٌ، حَتَّى يَسْتَقِلَّ الظِّلُّ بِالرُّمْحِ. ثُمَّ أَقْصِرْ عَنِ الصَّلَاةِ؛ فَإِنَّ حِينَئِذٍ تُسْجَرُ جَهَنَّمُ. فَإِذَا أَقْبَلَ الْفَيْءُ فَصَلِّ؛ فَإِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ مَشْهُودَةٌ مَحْضُورَةٌ، حَتَّى تُصَلِّيَ الْعَصْرَ. ثُمَّ أَقْصِرْ عَنِ الصَّلَاةِ حَتَّى تَغْرُبَ الشَّمْسُ؛ فَإِنَّهَا تَغْرُبُ بَيْنَ قَرْنَيْ شَيْطَانٍ، وَحِينَئِذٍ يَسْجُدُ لَهَا الْكُفَّارُ».
قال: فقلت: يا نبي الله، فالوضوء؟ حدثني عنه.
قال:
«مَا مِنْكُمْ رَجُلٌ يُقَرِّبُ وَضُوءَهُ، فَيَتَمَضْمَضُ وَيَسْتَنْشِقُ فَيَنْتَثِرُ، إِلَّا خَرَّتْ خَطَايَا وَجْهِهِ وَفِيهِ وَخَيَاشِيمِهِ، ثُمَّ إِذَا غَسَلَ وَجْهَهُ كَمَا أَمَرَهُ اللهُ، إِلَّا خَرَّتْ خَطَايَا وَجْهِهِ مِنْ أَطْرَافِ لِحْيَتِهِ مَعَ الْمَاءِ، ثُمَّ يَغْسِلُ يَدَيْهِ إِلَى الْمِرْفَقَيْنِ، إِلَّا خَرَّتْ خَطَايَا يَدَيْهِ مِنْ أَنَامِلِهِ مَعَ الْمَاءِ، ثُمَّ يَمْسَحُ رَأْسَهُ، إِلَّا خَرَّتْ خَطَايَا رَأْسِهِ مِنْ أَطْرَافِ شَعْرِهِ مَعَ الْمَاءِ، ثُمَّ يَغْسِلُ قَدَمَيْهِ إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ، إِلَّا خَرَّتْ خَطَايَا رِجْلَيْهِ مِنْ أَنَامِلِهِ مَعَ الْمَاءِ. فَإِنْ هُوَ قَامَ فَصَلَّى، فَحَمِدَ اللهَ وَأَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ وَمَجَّدَهُ بِالَّذِي هُوَ لَهُ أَهْلٌ، وَفَرَّغَ قَلْبَهُ لِلَّهِ، إِلَّا انْصَرَفَ مِنْ خَطِيئَتِهِ كَهَيْئَتِهِ يَوْمَ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ».
فحدث عمرو بن عبسة بهذا الحديث أبا أمامة صاحب رسول الله ﷺ، فقال له أبو أمامة: يا عمرو بن عبسة، انظر ما تقول، في مقام واحد يُعطى هذا الرجل؟
فقال عمرو: يا أبا أمامة، لقد كبرت سني، ورق عظمي، واقترب أجلي، وما بي حاجة أن أكذب على الله ولا على رسول الله ﷺ. لو لم أسمعه من رسول الله ﷺ إلا مرة أو مرتين أو ثلاثًا — حتى عد سبع مرات — ما حدثت به أبدًا، ولكني سمعته أكثر من ذلك.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٨٣٢).
وقوله: «يُقَرِّب وضوءه» — بفتح الواو — أي: الماء الذي يتوضأ به.

قال:
«نَعَمْ، أَنْتَ الَّذِي لَقِيتَنِي بِمَكَّةَ».
فقلت: بلى.
فقلت: يا نبي الله، أخبرني عما علمك الله وأجهله، أخبرني عن الصلاة.

قال:

وقوله: «يُقَرِّب وضوءه» — بفتح الواو — أي: الماء الذي يتوضأ به.

1558 — Abū Umāmah reported that ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah al-Sulamī said:
During the pre-Islamic period, I believed that the people were upon misguidance and had nothing of truth while they worshipped idols. Then I heard of a man in Makkah who was reporting extraordinary news, so I mounted my riding animal and went to him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was keeping himself concealed, while his people were acting boldly against him. I proceeded cautiously until I was able to meet him privately in Makkah.
I asked him:
“What are you?”
He said:
“I am a Prophet.”
I asked:
“What is a prophet?”
He said:
“Allah has sent me.”
I asked:
“With what has He sent you?”
He replied:
“He has sent me with maintaining ties of kinship, breaking the idols, and declaring Allah alone to be One, associating nothing with Him.”
I asked:
“Who is with you upon this?”
He replied:
“A free man and a slave.”
At that time Abū Bakr and Bilāl were among those who had believed in him.
I said:
“I will follow you.”
He replied:
“You are not able to do that on this day of yours. Do you not see my situation and the situation of the people? Rather, return to your family, and when you hear that I have become established, then come to me.”
So I returned to my family. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ later came to Madinah while I remained among my people. I continued seeking news and questioning people after he came to Madinah, until a group from Yathrib—the people of Madinah—came to me.
I asked:
“What has happened to the man who came to Madinah?”
They replied:
“People are rushing to him. His people tried to kill him but were unable to do so.”
So I went to Madinah and entered upon him.
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, do you recognize me?”
He replied:
“Yes. You are the one who met me in Makkah.”
I said:
“Yes.”
Then I said:
“O Prophet of Allah, tell me about what Allah has taught you and what I do not know. Tell me about the prayer.”
He said:
“Pray the dawn prayer, then refrain from prayer until the sun rises and becomes elevated, for when it rises it rises between the two horns of Satan, and at that time the disbelievers prostrate to it. Then pray, for the prayer is witnessed and attended, until the shadow becomes directly beneath the spear. Then refrain from prayer, for at that time Hell is kindled. When the shadow begins to return, then pray, for the prayer is witnessed and attended, until you have prayed ʿAṣr. Then refrain from prayer until the sun sets, for it sets between the two horns of Satan, and at that time the disbelievers prostrate to it.”
I then asked:
“O Prophet of Allah, tell me about wuḍūʾ.”
He said:
“There is no man among you who brings his water for wuḍūʾ, then rinses his mouth, draws water into his nose, and expels it, except that the sins of his face, his mouth, and his nostrils fall away.
Then, when he washes his face as Allah has commanded him, the sins of his face fall from the ends of his beard with the water.
Then he washes his hands up to the elbows, and the sins of his hands fall from his fingertips with the water.
Then he wipes his head, and the sins of his head fall from the ends of his hair with the water.
Then he washes his feet up to the ankles, and the sins of his feet fall from his toes with the water.
Then, if he stands and prays, praises Allah, extols Him, glorifies Him as He deserves, and empties his heart entirely for Allah, he departs from his sins in the same state as on the day his mother gave birth to him.”
ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah then narrated this hadith to Abū Umāmah, the Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Abū Umāmah said:
“O ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah, consider carefully what you are saying! Is a man granted all of this in a single occasion?”
ʿAmr replied:
“O Abū Umāmah, I have grown old, my bones have become frail, and my death has drawn near. I have no need to lie about Allah or about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Had I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only once, twice, or three times”—until he counted seven times—“I would never have narrated it. Rather, I heard it more times than that.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (832).
His statement, “he brings his wuḍūʾ,” with the wāw carrying a fatḥah, means the water with which he performs wuḍūʾ.

١٥٥٨ — عن أبي أمامة قال: قال عمرو بن عبسة السلمي: كنت وأنا في الجاهلية أظن أن الناس على ضلالة، وأنهم ليسوا على شيء وهم يعبدون الأوثان، فسمعت برجل بمكة يخبر أخبارًا، فقعدت على راحلتي، فقدمت عليه، فإذا رسول الله ﷺ مستخفٍ، جُرَآءُ عليه قومه، فتلطفت حتى دخلت عليه بمكة، فقلت له: ما أنت؟
قال:
«أَنَا نَبِيٌّ».
فقلت: وما نبي؟
قال:
«أَرْسَلَنِي اللهُ».
فقلت: وبأي شيء أرسلك؟
قال:
«أَرْسَلَنِي بِصِلَةِ الْأَرْحَامِ، وَكَسْرِ الْأَوْثَانِ، وَأَنْ يُوَحَّدَ اللهُ لَا يُشْرَكُ بِهِ شَيْءٌ».
قلت: فمن معك على هذا؟
قال:
«حُرٌّ وَعَبْدٌ».
قال: ومعه يومئذ أبو بكر وبلال ممن آمن به.
فقلت: إني متبعك.
قال:
«إِنَّكَ لَا تَسْتَطِيعُ ذَلِكَ يَوْمَكَ هَذَا، أَلَا تَرَى حَالِي وَحَالَ النَّاسِ؟ وَلَكِنِ ارْجِعْ إِلَى أَهْلِكَ، فَإِذَا سَمِعْتَ بِي قَدْ ظَهَرْتُ فَأْتِنِي».
قال: فذهبت إلى أهلي، وقدم رسول الله ﷺ المدينة، وكنت في أهلي، فجعلت أتخبر الأخبار وأسأل الناس حين قدم المدينة، حتى قدم علي نفر من أهل يثرب — من أهل المدينة — فقلت: ما فعل هذا الرجل الذي قدم المدينة؟
فقالوا: الناس إليه سراع، وقد أراد قومه قتله فلم يستطيعوا ذلك.
فقدمت المدينة، فدخلت عليه، فقلت: يا رسول الله، أتعرفني؟
قال:
«نَعَمْ، أَنْتَ الَّذِي لَقِيتَنِي بِمَكَّةَ».
فقلت: بلى.
فقلت: يا نبي الله، أخبرني عما علمك الله وأجهله، أخبرني عن الصلاة.
قال:
«صَلِّ صَلَاةَ الصُّبْحِ، ثُمَّ أَقْصِرْ عَنِ الصَّلَاةِ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ حَتَّى تَرْتَفِعَ؛ فَإِنَّهَا تَطْلُعُ حِينَ تَطْلُعُ بَيْنَ قَرْنَيْ شَيْطَانٍ، وَحِينَئِذٍ يَسْجُدُ لَهَا الْكُفَّارُ. ثُمَّ صَلِّ؛ فَإِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ مَشْهُودَةٌ مَحْضُورَةٌ، حَتَّى يَسْتَقِلَّ الظِّلُّ بِالرُّمْحِ. ثُمَّ أَقْصِرْ عَنِ الصَّلَاةِ؛ فَإِنَّ حِينَئِذٍ تُسْجَرُ جَهَنَّمُ. فَإِذَا أَقْبَلَ الْفَيْءُ فَصَلِّ؛ فَإِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ مَشْهُودَةٌ مَحْضُورَةٌ، حَتَّى تُصَلِّيَ الْعَصْرَ. ثُمَّ أَقْصِرْ عَنِ الصَّلَاةِ حَتَّى تَغْرُبَ الشَّمْسُ؛ فَإِنَّهَا تَغْرُبُ بَيْنَ قَرْنَيْ شَيْطَانٍ، وَحِينَئِذٍ يَسْجُدُ لَهَا الْكُفَّارُ».
قال: فقلت: يا نبي الله، فالوضوء؟ حدثني عنه.
قال:
«مَا مِنْكُمْ رَجُلٌ يُقَرِّبُ وَضُوءَهُ، فَيَتَمَضْمَضُ وَيَسْتَنْشِقُ فَيَنْتَثِرُ، إِلَّا خَرَّتْ خَطَايَا وَجْهِهِ وَفِيهِ وَخَيَاشِيمِهِ، ثُمَّ إِذَا غَسَلَ وَجْهَهُ كَمَا أَمَرَهُ اللهُ، إِلَّا خَرَّتْ خَطَايَا وَجْهِهِ مِنْ أَطْرَافِ لِحْيَتِهِ مَعَ الْمَاءِ، ثُمَّ يَغْسِلُ يَدَيْهِ إِلَى الْمِرْفَقَيْنِ، إِلَّا خَرَّتْ خَطَايَا يَدَيْهِ مِنْ أَنَامِلِهِ مَعَ الْمَاءِ، ثُمَّ يَمْسَحُ رَأْسَهُ، إِلَّا خَرَّتْ خَطَايَا رَأْسِهِ مِنْ أَطْرَافِ شَعْرِهِ مَعَ الْمَاءِ، ثُمَّ يَغْسِلُ قَدَمَيْهِ إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ، إِلَّا خَرَّتْ خَطَايَا رِجْلَيْهِ مِنْ أَنَامِلِهِ مَعَ الْمَاءِ. فَإِنْ هُوَ قَامَ فَصَلَّى، فَحَمِدَ اللهَ وَأَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ وَمَجَّدَهُ بِالَّذِي هُوَ لَهُ أَهْلٌ، وَفَرَّغَ قَلْبَهُ لِلَّهِ، إِلَّا انْصَرَفَ مِنْ خَطِيئَتِهِ كَهَيْئَتِهِ يَوْمَ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ».
فحدث عمرو بن عبسة بهذا الحديث أبا أمامة صاحب رسول الله ﷺ، فقال له أبو أمامة: يا عمرو بن عبسة، انظر ما تقول، في مقام واحد يُعطى هذا الرجل؟
فقال عمرو: يا أبا أمامة، لقد كبرت سني، ورق عظمي، واقترب أجلي، وما بي حاجة أن أكذب على الله ولا على رسول الله ﷺ. لو لم أسمعه من رسول الله ﷺ إلا مرة أو مرتين أو ثلاثًا — حتى عد سبع مرات — ما حدثت به أبدًا، ولكني سمعته أكثر من ذلك.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٨٣٢).
وقوله: «يُقَرِّب وضوءه» — بفتح الواو — أي: الماء الذي يتوضأ به.
1558 — Abū Umāmah reported that ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah al-Sulamī said:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was keeping himself concealed, while his people were acting boldly against him. I proceeded cautiously until I was able to meet him privately in Makkah.
I asked him:
“What are you?”
He said:
“I am a Prophet.”
I asked:
“What is a prophet?”
He said:
“Allah has sent me.”
I asked:
“With what has He sent you?”
He replied:
“He has sent me with maintaining ties of kinship, breaking the idols, and declaring Allah alone to be One, associating nothing with Him.”
I asked:
“Who is with you upon this?”
He replied:
“A free man and a slave.”
At that time Abū Bakr and Bilāl were among those who had believed in him.
I said:
“I will follow you.”
He replied:
“You are not able to do that on this day of yours. Do you not see my situation and the situation of the people? Rather, return to your family, and when you hear that I have become established, then come to me.”

I asked:

They replied:
“People are rushing to him. His people tried to kill him but were unable to do so.”

I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, do you recognize me?”
He replied:
“Yes. You are the one who met me in Makkah.”
I said:
“Yes.”
Then I said:
“O Prophet of Allah, tell me about what Allah has taught you and what I do not know. Tell me about the prayer.”
He said:
“Pray the dawn prayer, then refrain from prayer until the sun rises and becomes elevated, for when it rises it rises between the two horns of Satan, and at that time the disbelievers prostrate to it. Then pray, for the prayer is witnessed and attended, until the shadow becomes directly beneath the spear. Then refrain from prayer, for at that time Hell is kindled. When the shadow begins to return, then pray, for the prayer is witnessed and attended, until you have prayed ʿAṣr. Then refrain from prayer until the sun sets, for it sets between the two horns of Satan, and at that time the disbelievers prostrate to it.”
I then asked:
“O Prophet of Allah, tell me about wuḍūʾ.”
He said:
“There is no man among you who brings his water for wuḍūʾ, then rinses his mouth, draws water into his nose, and expels it, except that the sins of his face, his mouth, and his nostrils fall away.
Then, when he washes his face as Allah has commanded him, the sins of his face fall from the ends of his beard with the water.
Then he washes his hands up to the elbows, and the sins of his hands fall from his fingertips with the water.
Then he wipes his head, and the sins of his head fall from the ends of his hair with the water.
Then he washes his feet up to the ankles, and the sins of his feet fall from his toes with the water.
Then, if he stands and prays, praises Allah, extols Him, glorifies Him as He deserves, and empties his heart entirely for Allah, he departs from his sins in the same state as on the day his mother gave birth to him.”
ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah then narrated this hadith to Abū Umāmah, the Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Abū Umāmah said:

ʿAmr replied:
“O Abū Umāmah, I have grown old, my bones have become frail, and my death has drawn near. I have no need to lie about Allah or about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Had I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only once, twice, or three times”—until he counted seven times—“I would never have narrated it. Rather, I heard it more times than that.”

١٥٥٩ — عن أبي أمامة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«مَنْ خَرَجَ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ مُتَطَهِّرًا إِلَى صَلَاةٍ مَكْتُوبَةٍ فَأَجْرُهُ كَأَجْرِ الْحَاجِّ الْمُحْرِمِ، وَمَنْ خَرَجَ إِلَى تَسْبِيحِ الضُّحَى لَا يَنْصِبُهُ إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ فَأَجْرُهُ كَأَجْرِ الْمُعْتَمِرِ، وَصَلَاةٌ عَلَى إِثْرِ صَلَاةٍ لَا لَغْوَ بَيْنَهُمَا كِتَابٌ فِي عِلِّيِّينَ».
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٥٥٨).

1559 — Abū Umāmah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever leaves his house in a state of purification for an obligatory prayer will have a reward like that of a pilgrim in iḥrām. Whoever goes out for the prayer of Ḍuḥā, with nothing causing him to go out except it, will have a reward like that of one performing ʿumrah. And one prayer following another, with no idle speech between them, is recorded in ʿIlliyyīn.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (558).

1560 — Abū Umāmah, the Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—and ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said: Abū Umāmah al-Ḥimṣī, the Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Wuḍūʾ expiates what came before it, and then the prayer becomes an additional voluntary deed.”
I asked him:
“Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?”

١٥٦١ — عن عقبة بن عامر قال: سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول:
«رَجُلَانِ مِنْ أُمَّتِي، يَقُومُ أَحَدُهُمَا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ يُعَالِجُ نَفْسَهُ إِلَى الطَّهُورِ، وَعَلَيْهِ عُقَدٌ، فَيَتَوَضَّأُ، فَإِذَا وَضَّأَ يَدَيْهِ انْحَلَّتْ عُقْدَةٌ، وَإِذَا وَضَّأَ وَجْهَهُ انْحَلَّتْ عُقْدَةٌ، وَإِذَا مَسَحَ بِرَأْسِهِ انْحَلَّتْ عُقْدَةٌ، وَإِذَا وَضَّأَ رِجْلَيْهِ انْحَلَّتْ عُقْدَةٌ، فَيَقُولُ اللهُ لِلَّذِينَ وَرَاءَ الْحِجَابِ: انْظُرُوا إِلَى عَبْدِي هَذَا يُعَالِجُ نَفْسَهُ يَسْأَلُنِي، مَا سَأَلَنِي عَبْدِي فَهُوَ لَهُ».

1561 — ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
“Two men from my Ummah: one of them rises during the night, struggling against himself to reach the water of purification while knots are upon him. He performs wuḍūʾ. When he washes his hands, one knot is undone; when he washes his face, one knot is undone; when he wipes his head, one knot is undone; and when he washes his feet, one knot is undone.
Then Allah says to those behind the veil: ‘Look at this servant of Mine. He struggles against himself and asks Me. Whatever My servant asks of Me is his.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (17791) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (17/301). This wording is that of Aḥmad.

١٥٦٢ — عن أبي هريرة أن النبي ﷺ قال لبلال عند صلاة الفجر:
«يَا بِلَالُ، حَدِّثْنِي بِأَرْجَى عَمَلٍ عَمِلْتَهُ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ؛ فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ دَفَّ نَعْلَيْكَ بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ فِي الْجَنَّةِ».
قال: ما عملت عملًا أرجى عندي أني لم أتطهر طهورًا في ساعة ليل أو نهار إلا صليت بذلك الطهور ما كتب لي أن أصلي.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١١٤٩)، ومسلم (٢٤٥٨)، واللفظ للبخاري.
وفي لفظ مسلم:
«يَا بِلَالُ، حَدِّثْنِي بِأَرْجَى عَمَلٍ عَمِلْتَهُ عِنْدَكَ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ مَنْفَعَةً؛ فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ اللَّيْلَةَ خَشْفَ نَعْلَيْكَ بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ فِي الْجَنَّةِ».

1562 — Abū Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said to Bilāl at the time of the dawn prayer:
“O Bilāl, tell me about the deed you have done in Islam for which you have the greatest hope, for I heard the sound of your sandals before me in Paradise.”
Bilāl replied:
“I have done no deed for which I have greater hope than this: whenever I purified myself at any hour of the night or day, I prayed with that purification whatever was decreed for me to pray.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1149) and Muslim (2458). This wording is that of al-Bukhārī.
In Muslim’s wording:
“O Bilāl, tell me about the deed you have done in Islam that you consider most beneficial, for tonight I heard the soft sound of your sandals before me in Paradise.”

١٥٦٣ — عن حُمران مولى عثمان بن عفان، أن عثمان بن عفان جلس على المقاعد، فجاء المؤذن فآذنه بصلاة العصر، فدعا بماء فتوضأ، ثم قال: والله لأحدثنكم حديثًا، لولا أنه في كتاب الله ما حدثتكموه.
ثم قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«مَا مِنِ امْرِئٍ يَتَوَضَّأُ فَيُحْسِنُ الْوُضُوءَ، ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي الصَّلَاةَ، إِلَّا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الصَّلَاةِ الْأُخْرَى حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَهَا».

١٥٦٤ — عن أبي هريرة أنه سمع رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«أَرَأَيْتُمْ لَوْ أَنَّ نَهَرًا بِبَابِ أَحَدِكُمْ يَغْتَسِلُ فِيهِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ خَمْسًا، مَا تَقُولُ ذَلِكَ يُبْقِي مِنْ دَرَنِهِ؟»
قالوا: لا يبقي من درنه شيئًا.
قال:
«فَذَلِكَ مَثَلُ الصَّلَوَاتِ الْخَمْسِ؛ يَمْحُو اللهُ بِهِنَّ الْخَطَايَا».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٢٨)، ومسلم (٦٦٧).
وفي رواية:
«مَثَلُ الصَّلَوَاتِ الْخَمْسِ كَمَثَلِ نَهَرٍ جَارٍ عَلَى بَابِ أَحَدِكُمْ يَغْتَسِلُ مِنْهُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ خَمْسَ مَرَّاتٍ، فَمَا يُبْقِينَ مِنْ دَرَنِهِ؟»

1564 — Abū Hurayrah reported that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Tell me: if there were a river at the door of one of you in which he bathed five times every day, would any of his dirt remain?”
They replied:
“None of his dirt would remain.”
He said:
“That is the likeness of the five daily prayers: Allah wipes away sins through them.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (528) and Muslim (667).
In another wording:
“The likeness of the five prayers is that of a flowing river at the door of one of you in which he bathes five times every day. What would they leave of his dirt?”

1567 — Saʿd and a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reported:
There were two brothers during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. One of them was more virtuous than the other. The more virtuous of the two died, and the other lived for forty nights after him and then died.
The superiority of the first over the second was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said:
“Was he not praying?”
They replied:
“Yes, O Messenger of Allah, and there was nothing wrong with him.”
He said:
“How do you know how far his prayer raised him?”
Then he said:
“The likeness of prayer is that of a deep, sweet, flowing river at the door of a man into which he plunges five times every day. What do you think that would leave of his dirt?”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (1534); authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (310) and al-Ḥākim (1/200).
A ghamr river means a river abundant in water.

١٥٦٨ — عن علي قال: كنت إذا سمعت من رسول الله ﷺ حديثًا نفعني الله بما شاء منه، وإذا حدثني عنه غيري استحلفته، فإذا حلف لي صدقته.
وإن أبا بكر حدثني — وصدق أبو بكر — أنه سمع النبي ﷺ قال:
«مَا مِنْ رَجُلٍ يُذْنِبُ ذَنْبًا، فَيَتَوَضَّأُ فَيُحْسِنُ الْوُضُوءَ، ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ، وَيَسْتَغْفِرُ اللهَ، إِلَّا غَفَرَ اللهُ لَهُ».
ثم قرأ هذه الآية:
﴿وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا فَعَلُوا فَاحِشَةً أَوْ ظَلَمُوا أَنفُسَهُمْ ذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ فَاسْتَغْفَرُوا لِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَمَن يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَلَمْ يُصِرُّوا عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلُوا وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [آل عمران: ١٣٥].
حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٥٢١)، والترمذي في تفسير سورة آل عمران (٣٠٠٦) وحسنه، وابن ماجه (١٣٩٥).

1568 — ʿAlī said: Whenever I heard a hadith directly from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Allah benefited me through it as He willed. When someone else narrated to me from him, I would ask him to swear an oath; if he swore to me, I believed him.
Abū Bakr narrated to me—and Abū Bakr spoke the truth—that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
“No man commits a sin, then performs wuḍūʾ and perfects his wuḍūʾ, then prays two rakʿahs and asks Allah for forgiveness, except that Allah forgives him.”
He then recited this verse:
“And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins—and who can forgive sins except Allah?—and they do not knowingly persist in what they have done.” [Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:135]
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1521), al-Tirmidhī in his Tafsīr of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān (3006), who graded it Ḥasan, and Ibn Mājah (1395).

“No man commits a sin, then performs wuḍūʾ and perfects his wuḍūʾ, then prays two rakʿahs and asks Allah for forgiveness, except that Allah forgives him.”
He then recited this verse:
“And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins—and who can forgive sins except Allah?—and they do not knowingly persist in what they have done.” [Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:135]
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1521), al-Tirmidhī in his Tafsīr of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān (3006), who graded it Ḥasan, and Ibn Mājah (1395).

«مَنْ تَوَضَّأَ فَأَحْسَنَ وُضُوءَهُ، ثُمَّ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ لَا يَسْهُو فِيهِمَا، غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ».

١٥٧٠ — عن ثوبان قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«سَدِّدُوا وَقَارِبُوا وَاعْمَلُوا، وَخَيْرُ أَعْمَالِكُمُ الصَّلَاةُ، وَلَا يُحَافِظُ عَلَى الْوُضُوءِ إِلَّا مُؤْمِنٌ».
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٢٤٣٣)، والطبراني في المعجم الكبير (١٤٤٤).

1570 — Thawbān reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Be upright, strive to come close to what is right, and perform good deeds. The best of your deeds is prayer, and no one consistently maintains wuḍūʾ except a believer.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (22433) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (1444).

١٥٧١ — عن أبي هريرة قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«إِنَّ أُمَّتِي يُدْعَوْنَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ غُرًّا مُحَجَّلِينَ مِنْ آثَارِ الْوُضُوءِ؛ فَمَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يُطِيلَ غُرَّتَهُ فَلْيَفْعَلْ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٣٦)، واللفظ له، ومسلم (٢٤٦).
وقوله: «غُرًّا مُحَجَّلين»: الغُرَّة والتحجيل بياض في وجه الفرس وقوائمه، وذلك مما يحسنه ويزينه، فاستُعير ذلك للإنسان، فجُعل أثر الوضوء في الوجه واليدين والرجلين كالبياض الذي يكون في الفرس. ولذلك جاء الحث على إسباغ الوضوء؛ فإنه يزيد التحجيل ويطيله.
وتطويل الغُرَّة والتحجيل المقصود منه الزيادة على القدر الذي يجب غسله.

1571 — Abū Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“My Ummah will be summoned on the Day of Resurrection with bright faces and bright limbs from the traces of wuḍūʾ. So whoever among you is able to extend his brightness, let him do so.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (136), whose wording this is, and Muslim (246).
The expression “bright-faced and bright-limbed” comes from the ghurrah and taḥjīl of a horse: whiteness upon its face and legs that beautifies and adorns it. The expression is used metaphorically for a person, so that the traces of wuḍūʾ upon the face, hands, and feet are likened to the white markings of a horse.
For this reason, thorough completion of wuḍūʾ is encouraged, as it increases and extends this brightness.
Extending the ghurrah and taḥjīl refers to washing beyond the minimum area that is obligatory to wash.

١٥٧٢ — عن أبي حازم قال: كنت خلف أبي هريرة وهو يتوضأ للصلاة، فكان يمد يده حتى تبلغ إبطه، فقلت له: ما هذا يا أبا هريرة؟
فقال: يا بني فَرُّوخ! أنتم هاهنا؟ لو علمت أنكم هاهنا ما توضأت هذا الوضوء. سمعت النبي ﷺ، خليلي، يقول:
«تَبْلُغُ الْحِلْيَةُ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ حَيْثُ يَبْلُغُ الْوُضُوءُ».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٥٠).

1572 — Abū Ḥāzim said: I was behind Abū Hurayrah while he was performing wuḍūʾ for prayer. He continued washing his arm until he reached his armpit.
I asked him:
“What is this, O Abū Hurayrah?”
He replied:
“O sons of Farrūkh! Are you here? Had I known that you were here, I would not have performed wuḍūʾ in this manner. I heard the Prophet ﷺ, my beloved, say:
‘The adornment of the believer will reach as far as his wuḍūʾ reaches.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (250).

١٥٧٣ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ خرج إلى المقبرة فقال:
«السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ دَارَ قَوْمٍ مُؤْمِنِينَ، وَإِنَّا إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ بِكُمْ لَاحِقُونَ، وَدِدْتُ أَنِّي قَدْ رَأَيْتُ إِخْوَانَنَا».
فقالوا: يا رسول الله، ألسنا بإخوانك؟
قال:
«بَلْ أَنْتُمْ أَصْحَابِي، وَإِخْوَانُنَا الَّذِينَ لَمْ يَأْتُوا بَعْدُ، وَأَنَا فَرَطُهُمْ عَلَى الْحَوْضِ».
فقالوا: يا رسول الله، كيف تعرف من يأتي بعدك من أمتك؟
قال:
«أَرَأَيْتَ لَوْ كَانَ لِرَجُلٍ خَيْلٌ غُرٌّ مُحَجَّلَةٌ فِي خَيْلٍ دُهْمٍ بُهْمٍ، أَلَا يَعْرِفُ خَيْلَهُ؟»
قالوا: بلى يا رسول الله.
قال:
«فَإِنَّهُمْ يَأْتُونَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ غُرًّا مُحَجَّلِينَ مِنَ الْوُضُوءِ، وَأَنَا فَرَطُهُمْ عَلَى الْحَوْضِ، فَلَيُذَادَنَّ رِجَالٌ عَنْ حَوْضِي كَمَا يُذَادُ الْبَعِيرُ الضَّالُّ، أُنَادِيهِمْ: أَلَا هَلُمَّ! أَلَا هَلُمَّ! أَلَا هَلُمَّ! فَيُقَالُ: إِنَّهُمْ قَدْ بَدَّلُوا بَعْدَكَ، فَأَقُولُ: فَسُحْقًا، فَسُحْقًا، فَسُحْقًا».
صحيح: رواه مالك (٢٨).

english_source:
1573 — Abū Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the graveyard and said:
“Peace be upon you, abode of believing people. Indeed, if Allah wills, we will join you. I wish that I had seen our brothers.”
They said:
“O Messenger of Allah, are we not your brothers?”
He said:
“Rather, you are my Companions. Our brothers are those who have not yet come, and I will precede them at the Basin.”
They asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize those of your Ummah who come after you?”
He said:
“Tell me: if a man owned horses with white blazes and white markings on their legs among completely black horses, would he not recognize his own horses?”
They replied:
“Yes, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“They will come on the Day of Resurrection with bright faces and bright limbs from wuḍūʾ, and I will precede them at the Basin. Men will certainly be driven away from my Basin just as a stray camel is driven away. I will call to them: ‘Come! Come! Come!’ Then it will be said: ‘They changed after you.’ So I will say: ‘Away with them! Away with them! Away with them!’”
Authentic: Narrated by Mālik (28).

١٥٧٤ — عن حذيفة قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«إِنَّ حَوْضِي لَأَبْعَدُ مِنْ أَيْلَةَ مِنْ عَدَنَ، وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ! إِنِّي لَأَذُودُ عَنْهُ الرِّجَالَ كَمَا يَذُودُ الرَّجُلُ الْإِبِلَ الْغَرِيبَةَ مِنْ حَوْضِهِ».
قالوا: يا رسول الله، وتعرفنا؟
قال:
«نَعَمْ، تَرِدُونَ عَلَيَّ غُرًّا مُحَجَّلِينَ مِنْ آثَارِ الْوُضُوءِ، لَيْسَتْ لِأَحَدٍ غَيْرِكُمْ».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤٨).

english_source:
1574 — Ḥudhayfah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“My Basin is farther in extent than the distance between Aylah and ʿAdan. By the One in whose Hand is my soul, I will drive men away from it just as a man drives unfamiliar camels away from his watering place.”
They asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, will you recognize us?”
He replied:
“Yes. You will come to me with bright faces and bright limbs from the traces of wuḍūʾ, a distinction belonging to no one other than you.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (248).

arabic_source:
١٥٧٥ — عن عبد الله بن بُسر، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
«أُمَّتِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ غُرٌّ مِنَ السُّجُودِ، مُحَجَّلُونَ مِنَ الْوُضُوءِ».
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٦٠٧)، وقال: «هذا حديث حسن صحيح غريب».
ورواه أحمد (١٧٦٩٣)، والطبراني في مسند الشاميين (٩٩٥) بلفظ:
«مَا مِنْ أُمَّتِي مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا أَنَا أَعْرِفُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ».
قالوا: وكيف تعرفهم يا رسول الله في كثرة الخلائق؟
قال:
«أَرَأَيْتَ لَوْ دَخَلْتَ حَظِيرَةً فِيهَا خَيْلٌ دُهْمٌ بُهْمٌ، وَفِيهَا فَرَسٌ أَغَرُّ مُحَجَّلٌ، أَمَا كُنْتَ تَعْرِفُهُ مِنْهَا؟»
قالوا: بلى.
قال:
«فَإِنَّ أُمَّتِي يَوْمَئِذٍ غُرٌّ مِنَ السُّجُودِ، مُحَجَّلُونَ مِنَ الْوُضُوءِ».
وقوله: «بُهْمٌ» — بضم الباء وسكون الهاء — أي: خالصة السواد.

١٥٧٦ — عن ابن مسعود قال: قيل: يا رسول الله، كيف تعرف من لم تر من أمتك؟
قال:
«غُرٌّ مُحَجَّلُونَ بُلْقٌ مِنْ آثَارِ الْوُضُوءِ».
حسن: رواه ابن ماجه (٢٨٤)، وابن حبان في صحيحه (١٠٤٧).
وقوله: «بُلْقٌ»: من بَلِقَ الفرس بَلَقًا وبُلْقَةً إذا كان فيه سواد وبياض.

english_source:
1576 — Ibn Masʿūd said: It was asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize those of your Ummah whom you have never seen?”
He replied:
“They will be bright-faced and bright-limbed, marked with brightness from the traces of wuḍūʾ.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (284) and Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ (1047).
The word “bulq” derives from describing a horse as ablaq when its coloring contains both black and white.

١٥٧٧ — عن عائشة قالت: كان النبي ﷺ يعجبه التيمُّن في تنعله، وترجله، وطهوره، وفي شأنه كله.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٦٨)، ومسلم (٢٦٨).
ورواه مسلم بلفظ:
«إِنْ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ لَيُحِبُّ التَّيَمُّنَ فِي طُهُورِهِ إِذَا تَطَهَّرَ، وَفِي تَرَجُّلِهِ إِذَا تَرَجَّلَ، وَفِي انْتِعَالِهِ إِذَا انْتَعَلَ».

english_source:
1577 — ʿĀʾishah said: The Prophet ﷺ liked beginning with the right side when putting on his sandals, combing his hair, performing purification, and in all of his affairs.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (168) and Muslim (268).
Muslim also narrated:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved beginning with the right side in his purification when he purified himself, in combing his hair when he combed it, and in putting on his sandals when he put them on.”

١٥٧٩ — عن عمرو بن يحيى المازني، عن أبيه، أنه قال لعبد الله بن زيد بن عاصم — وهو جد عمرو بن يحيى المازني، وكان من أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ —: هل تستطيع أن تريني كيف كان رسول الله ﷺ يتوضأ؟
فقال عبد الله بن زيد بن عاصم: نعم.
فدعا بوَضوء، فأفرغ على يديه، فغسل يديه مرتين مرتين، ثم تمضمض واستنثر ثلاثًا، ثم غسل وجهه ثلاثًا، ثم غسل يديه مرتين مرتين إلى المرفقين، ثم مسح رأسه بيديه، فأقبل بهما وأدبر؛ بدأ بمقدم رأسه، ثم ذهب بهما إلى قفاه، ثم ردهما حتى رجع إلى المكان الذي بدأ منه، ثم غسل رجليه.
متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٣٢)، والبخاري (١٨٥)، ومسلم (٢٣٥).

١٥٨٠ — عن ابن عباس أنه توضأ، فغسل وجهه، وأخذ غرفة من ماء فمضمض بها واستنشق، ثم أخذ غرفة من ماء فجعل بها هكذا، أضافها إلى يده الأخرى فغسل بهما وجهه، ثم أخذ غرفة من ماء فغسل بها يده اليمنى، ثم أخذ غرفة من ماء فغسل بها يده اليسرى، ثم مسح برأسه، ثم أخذ غرفة من ماء فرش على رجله اليمنى حتى غسلها، ثم أخذ غرفة أخرى فغسل بها رجله اليسرى، ثم قال:
هكذا رأيت رسول الله ﷺ يتوضأ.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٤٠).
وقال مرة:
«تَوَضَّأَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ مَرَّةً مَرَّةً».
رواه البخاري أيضًا (١٥٧).
هكذا رواه جمع من الرواة عن ابن عباس أن النبي ﷺ توضأ مرة مرة. واتفق أهل العلم أن الوضوء يجزئ مرة مرة، ومرتين مرتين، وثلاث مرات، وثبت عن النبي ﷺ كل ذلك، كما ثبت أنه توضأ بعض وضوئه مرة، وبعضه ثلاثًا.

english_source:
1580 — Ibn ʿAbbās performed wuḍūʾ. He took a handful of water, rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose. He then took another handful, joined it with his other hand, and washed his face with both hands.
He took a handful of water and washed his right arm, then another handful and washed his left arm. He then wiped his head.
After that, he took a handful of water and poured it over his right foot until he washed it, then took another handful and washed his left foot.
He then said:
“This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform wuḍūʾ.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (140).
In another report:
“The Prophet ﷺ performed wuḍūʾ once for each limb.”
Also narrated by al-Bukhārī (157).
A number of narrators reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet ﷺ performed wuḍūʾ once for each limb. The scholars agreed that wuḍūʾ is valid when each limb is washed once, twice, or three times. All of these forms are authentically established from the Prophet ﷺ. It is also established that on some occasions he washed some limbs once and others three times.

١٥٨١ — عن حُمران مولى عثمان أنه أخبر أنه رأى عثمان بن عفان دعا بإناء، فأفرغ على كفيه ثلاث مرات فغسلهما، ثم أدخل يمينه في الإناء فمضمض واستنشق، ثم غسل وجهه ثلاثًا، ويديه إلى المرفقين ثلاث مرار، ثم مسح برأسه، ثم غسل رجليه ثلاث مرار إلى الكعبين.
ثم قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«مَنْ تَوَضَّأَ نَحْوَ وُضُوئِي هَذَا، ثُمَّ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ لَا يُحَدِّثُ فِيهِمَا نَفْسَهُ، غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٥٩)، واللفظ له، ومسلم (٢٢٦).

1581 — Ḥumrān, the freed servant of ʿUthmān, reported that he saw ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān call for a vessel of water.
He poured water over his hands three times and washed them. He then placed his right hand into the vessel, rinsed his mouth, and drew water into his nose.
He washed his face three times, his arms to the elbows three times, wiped his head, and then washed his feet to the ankles three times.
He then said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever performs wuḍūʾ in a manner similar to this wuḍūʾ of mine, then prays two rakʿahs without allowing himself to become distracted by thoughts during them, will have his previous sins forgiven.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (159), whose wording this is, and Muslim (226).

«مَنْ تَوَضَّأَ نَحْوَ وُضُوئِي هَذَا، ثُمَّ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ لَا يُحَدِّثُ فِيهِمَا نَفْسَهُ، غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٥٩)، واللفظ له، ومسلم (٢٢٦).
1581 — Ḥumrān, the freed servant of ʿUthmān, reported that he saw ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān call for a vessel of water.
He poured water over his hands three times and washed them. He then placed his right hand into the vessel, rinsed his mouth, and drew water into his nose.
He washed his face three times, his arms to the elbows three times, wiped his head, and then washed his feet to the ankles three times.
He then said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever performs wuḍūʾ in a manner similar to this wuḍūʾ of mine, then prays two rakʿahs without allowing himself to become distracted by thoughts during them, will have his previous sins forgiven.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (159), whose wording this is, and Muslim (226).

١٥٨٢ — عن عبد خير قال: أتانا علي رضي الله عنه وقد صلى، فدعا بطهور، فقلنا: ما يصنع بالطهور وقد صلى؟ ما يريد إلا ليعلمنا.

ثم قال:
من سره أن يعلم وضوء رسول الله ﷺ فهو هذا.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (١١١)، واللفظ له، والنسائي (٩٢).

1582 — ʿAbd Khayr said: ʿAlī may Allah be pleased with him came to us after he had already prayed and called for water for wuḍūʾ.
We said:
“What does he intend to do with water for wuḍūʾ when he has already prayed? He only intends to teach us.”
A vessel containing water and a basin were brought. He poured water from the vessel and washed his hands three times. He rinsed his mouth and expelled water from his nose three times, using the same handful for rinsing the mouth and nose.
He then washed his face three times, his right arm three times, and his left arm three times. He placed his hand into the vessel and wiped his head once. Then he washed his right foot three times and his left foot three times.
He said:
“Whoever would like to know the wuḍūʾ of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, this is it.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (111), whose wording this is, and al-Nasāʾī (92).

١٥٨٣ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده أن رجلًا أتى النبي ﷺ فقال: يا رسول الله، كيف الطهور؟
فدعا بماء في إناء، فغسل كفيه ثلاثًا، ثم غسل وجهه ثلاثًا، ثم غسل ذراعيه ثلاثًا، ثم مسح برأسه؛ فأدخل إصبعيه السباحتين في أذنيه، ومسح بإبهاميه على ظاهر أذنيه، وبالسباحتين باطن أذنيه، ثم غسل رجليه ثلاثًا ثلاثًا.
ثم قال:
«هَكَذَا الْوُضُوءُ؛ فَمَنْ زَادَ عَلَى هَذَا أَوْ نَقَصَ فَقَدْ أَسَاءَ وَظَلَمَ».
أو:
«ظَلَمَ وَأَسَاءَ».
حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٣٥)، واللفظ له، والنسائي (١٤٠)، وابن ماجه (٤٢٢).
ورواه النسائي وابن ماجه مختصرًا بلفظ:
«فَأَرَاهُ الْوُضُوءَ ثَلَاثًا ثَلَاثًا، ثُمَّ قَالَ: هَكَذَا الْوُضُوءُ؛ فَمَنْ زَادَ عَلَى هَذَا فَقَدْ أَسَاءَ وَتَعَدَّى وَظَلَمَ».
وقوله: «فمن زاد على هذا»؛ أي: في العدد.
وبوب ابن خزيمة (١٧٤) فقال: باب التغليظ في غسل أعضاء الوضوء أكثر من ثلاث، والدليل على أن فاعله مسيء ظالم، أو متعد ظالم. ثم ذكر الحديث.
وإلا فقد ثبت من حديث أبي هريرة غسل اليدين إلى المنكبين والرجلين إلى الساقين في حديث الغر المحجلين.
وأما ما ورد في رواية أبي داود: «أو نقص» — وقد تفرد بهذه الزيادة — فهو منكر؛ لجواز الوضوء مرة مرة، ومرتين مرتين.

english_source:
1583 — ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, how is purification performed?”
He called for water in a vessel and washed his hands three times, washed his face three times, and washed his forearms three times.
He then wiped his head, inserted his two index fingers into his ears, wiped the outer portions of his ears with his thumbs and their inner portions with his index fingers, and then washed his feet three times each.
He then said:
“This is wuḍūʾ. Whoever adds to this or falls short has acted badly and wronged.”
Or:
“Has wronged and acted badly.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (135), whose wording this is, al-Nasāʾī (140), and Ibn Mājah (422).
Al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah narrate a shorter wording:
“He showed him wuḍūʾ three times for each limb, then said: ‘This is wuḍūʾ. Whoever adds to this has acted badly, exceeded the limit, and wronged.’”
The statement “whoever adds to this” refers to increasing the number of washings.
Ibn Khuzaymah titled a chapter (174): “The stern warning concerning washing the limbs of wuḍūʾ more than three times, and the evidence that whoever does so is a wrongdoer who has acted badly, or an overstepping wrongdoer.” He then cited this hadith.
This does not contradict the established narration from Abū Hurayrah concerning washing the arms toward the shoulders and the legs toward the shins in connection with the bright-faced and bright-limbed.
As for the wording in Abū Dāwūd, “or falls short,” which occurs as an isolated addition in this wording, it is rejected, because wuḍūʾ is valid when the limbs are washed once each or twice each.

وبوب ابن خزيمة (١٧٤) فقال: باب التغليظ في غسل أعضاء الوضوء أكثر من ثلاث، والدليل على أن فاعله مسيء ظالم، أو متعد ظالم. ثم ذكر الحديث.
وإلا فقد ثبت من حديث أبي هريرة غسل اليدين إلى المنكبين والرجلين إلى الساقين في حديث الغر المحجلين.
وأما ما ورد في رواية أبي داود: «أو نقص» — وقد تفرد بهذه الزيادة — فهو منكر؛ لجواز الوضوء مرة مرة، ومرتين مرتين.
1583 — ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, how is purification performed?”
He called for water in a vessel and washed his hands three times, washed his face three times, and washed his forearms three times.
He then wiped his head, inserted his two index fingers into his ears, wiped the outer portions of his ears with his thumbs and their inner portions with his index fingers, and then washed his feet three times each.
He then said:
“This is wuḍūʾ. Whoever adds to this or falls short has acted badly and wronged.”
Or:
“Has wronged and acted badly.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (135), whose wording this is, al-Nasāʾī (140), and Ibn Mājah (422).
Al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah narrate a shorter wording:
“He showed him wuḍūʾ three times for each limb, then said: ‘This is wuḍūʾ. Whoever adds to this has acted badly, exceeded the limit, and wronged.’”
The statement “whoever adds to this” refers to increasing the number of washings.
Ibn Khuzaymah titled a chapter (174): “The stern warning concerning washing the limbs of wuḍūʾ more than three times, and the evidence that whoever does so is a wrongdoer who has acted badly, or an overstepping wrongdoer.” He then cited this hadith.
This does not contradict the established narration from Abū Hurayrah concerning washing the arms toward the shoulders and the legs toward the shins in connection with the bright-faced and bright-limbed.
As for the wording in Abū Dāwūd, “or falls short,” which occurs as an isolated addition in this wording, it is rejected, because wuḍūʾ is valid when the limbs are washed once each or twice each.

١٥٨٥ — عن الربيع بنت معوذ قالت: إن رسول الله ﷺ توضأ عندها، فمسح الرأس كله من قرن الشعر، كل ناحية لمنصب الشعر، لا يحرك الشعر عن هيئته.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٢٨).
وقولها: «فمسح الرأس كله» فيه دليل على تعميم مسح الرأس كله.

english_source:
1585 — Al-Rubayyiʿ bint Muʿawwidh reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed wuḍūʾ in her presence and wiped his entire head, beginning from the hairline and wiping each side in the direction in which the hair naturally lay, without disturbing the hair from its normal position.
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (128).
Her statement, “he wiped the entire head,” is evidence for wiping the whole head.

١٥٨٧ — عن المقدام بن معدي كرب الكندي قال: أُتي رسول الله ﷺ بوَضوء فتوضأ، فغسل كفيه ثلاثًا، وغسل وجهه ثلاثًا، ثم غسل ذراعيه ثلاثًا ثلاثًا، ثم تمضمض واستنشق ثلاثًا، ثم مسح برأسه وأذنيه ظاهرهما وباطنهما.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٢١).
وفي رواية أحمد: غسل كفيه ثلاثًا، وغسل وجهه ثلاثًا، ثم غسل ذراعيه ثلاثًا ثلاثًا، ثم تمضمض واستنشق ثلاثًا، ومسح برأسه وأذنيه ظاهرهما وباطنهما، وغسل رجليه ثلاثًا ثلاثًا.
رواه أحمد (١٧١٨٨).
والنكارة في رواية أحمد أن المضمضة والاستنشاق وقعا بعد غسل الذراعين، والمعروف في الأحاديث الصحيحة أنهما بعد غسل الكفين.

1587 — Al-Miqdām ibn Maʿdīkarib al-Kindī said: Water for wuḍūʾ was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He performed wuḍūʾ, washing his hands three times and his face three times, then washing his forearms three times each. He then rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose three times, and then wiped his head and his ears, both their outer and inner portions.
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (121).
In Aḥmad’s narration, he washed his hands three times and his face three times, then washed his forearms three times each, after which he rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose three times. He wiped his head and his ears, both their outer and inner portions, and washed his feet three times each.
Narrated by Aḥmad (17188).
The unusual feature in Aḥmad’s wording is that rinsing the mouth and nose occurs after washing the forearms, whereas the well-established order in the authentic narrations places them after washing the hands.

١٥٨٨ — عن أبي الأزهر المغيرة بن فروة ويزيد بن أبي مالك أن معاوية توضأ للناس كما رأى رسول الله ﷺ يتوضأ، فلما بلغ رأسه غرف غرفة من ماء فتلقاها بشماله حتى وضعها على وسط رأسه، حتى قطر الماء أو كان يقطر، ثم مسح من مقدمه إلى مؤخره، ومن مؤخره إلى مقدمه.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٢٤).

1588 — Abū al-Azhar al-Mughīrah ibn Furwah and Yazīd ibn Abī Mālik reported that Muʿāwiyah performed wuḍūʾ before the people in the manner in which he had seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform wuḍūʾ.
When he reached his head, he scooped a handful of water and received it with his left hand until he placed it upon the middle of his head, so that the water dripped—or was dripping.
He then wiped from the front of his head toward the back and from the back toward the front.
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (124).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٢٤).
1588 — Abū al-Azhar al-Mughīrah ibn Furwah and Yazīd ibn Abī Mālik reported that Muʿāwiyah performed wuḍūʾ before the people in the manner in which he had seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform wuḍūʾ.
When he reached his head, he scooped a handful of water and received it with his left hand until he placed it upon the middle of his head, so that the water dripped—or was dripping.
He then wiped from the front of his head toward the back and from the back toward the front.
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (124).

١٥٩٠ — عن البراء بن عازب أنه قال لبنيه: اجتمعوا فلأريكم كيف كان رسول الله ﷺ يتوضأ، وكيف كان يصلي؛ فإني لا أدري ما قدر صحبتي إياكم.
قال: فجمع بنيه وأهله، ودعا بوضوء، فمضمض واستنثر، وغسل وجهه ثلاثًا، وغسل اليد اليمنى ثلاثًا، وغسل يده هذه ثلاثًا — يعني اليسرى — ثم مسح رأسه وأذنيه ظاهرهما وباطنهما، وغسل هذه الرجل — يعني اليمنى — ثلاثًا، وغسل هذه الرجل ثلاثًا — يعني اليسرى.
قال: هكذا ما ألوت أن أريكم كيف كان رسول الله ﷺ يتوضأ.
ثم دخل بيته، فصلى صلاة لا ندري ما هي، ثم خرج فأمر بالصلاة، فأقيمت، فصلى بنا الظهر، فأحسب أني سمعت منه آيات من «يس»، ثم صلى العصر، ثم صلى بنا المغرب، ثم صلى بنا العشاء، وقال:
«ما ألوت أن أريكم كيف كان رسول الله ﷺ يتوضأ، وكيف كان يصلي».
حسن: رواه الإمام أحمد (١٨٥٣٧).

1590 — Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib said to his sons:
“Gather together so that I may show you how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform wuḍūʾ and how he used to pray, for I do not know how much longer I will remain in your company.”
He gathered his sons and family and called for water for wuḍūʾ. He rinsed his mouth and expelled water from his nose, washed his face three times, washed his right arm three times and his left arm three times, then wiped his head and his ears, both their outer and inner parts. He washed his right foot three times and his left foot three times.
He said:
“This is the utmost I can do to show you how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform wuḍūʾ.”
He then entered his house and prayed a prayer whose identity they did not know. Afterward he came out and ordered that the prayer be established. He led them in Ẓuhr, and al-Barāʾ said: “I think I heard him reciting verses from Sūrah Yā-Sīn.” He then prayed ʿAṣr, then led them in Maghrib, and then led them in ʿIshāʾ.
He said:
“This is the utmost I can do to show you how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform wuḍūʾ and how he used to pray.”
Good: Narrated by Imām Aḥmad (18537).

arabic_source:
١٥٩١ — عن المغيرة بن شعبة أنه سئل: هل أمَّ النبيَّ ﷺ أحد من هذه الأمة غير أبي بكر رضي الله عنه؟ فقال: نعم.
كنا مع النبي ﷺ في سفر، فلما كان من السحر ضرب عنق راحلتي، فظننت أن له حاجة، فعدلت معه، فانطلقنا حتى برزنا عن الناس، فنزل عن راحلته، ثم انطلق يتغيب عني حتى ما أراه، فمكث طويلًا، ثم جاء فقال:
«حاجتك يا مغيرة؟»
قلت: ما لي حاجة.
فقال:
«هل معك ماء؟»
فقلت: نعم.
فقمت إلى قربة، أو إلى سطيحة، معلقة في آخرة الرحل، فأتيته بماء، فصببت عليه، فغسل يديه فأحسن غسلهما — قال: وأشك أقال: دلكهما بتراب أم لا — ثم غسل وجهه.
ثم ذهب يحسر عن يديه وعليه جبة شامية ضيقة الكمين، فضاقت، فأخرج يديه من تحتها إخراجًا، فغسل وجهه ويديه — قال: فيجيء في الحديث غسل الوجه مرتين؟ قال: لا أدري ألكذا كان أم لا — ثم مسح بناصيته، ومسح على العمامة، ومسح على الخفين.
وركبنا فأدركنا القوم وقد أقيمت الصلاة، وقدموا عبد الرحمن بن عوف، وقد صلى بهم ركعة وهو في الثانية، فصففنا خلفه، فصلينا الركعة التي أدركنا، وقضينا الركعة التي سبقت.
صحيح: رواه الإمام أحمد (١٨١٣٤).

1591 — Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah was asked:
“Did anyone from this Ummah ever lead the Prophet ﷺ in prayer besides Abū Bakr may Allah be pleased with him?”
He replied: “Yes.”
We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey. In the latter part of the night, he struck the neck of my riding animal, and I thought that he had some need, so I turned aside with him. We continued until we were away from the people.
He dismounted and went off until he was hidden from my sight. He remained away for a long time, then returned and said:
“Do you have any need, O Mughīrah?”
I replied: “I have no need.”
He asked:
“Do you have water?”
I said: “Yes.”
I went to a waterskin—or another water container—hanging at the rear of the saddle and brought him water. I poured it for him, and he washed his hands thoroughly. The narrator said: “I am uncertain whether he said that he rubbed them with earth or not.”
He then washed his face. He tried to uncover his arms while wearing a Syrian cloak with tight sleeves, but the sleeves were too narrow, so he brought his arms out from beneath the cloak and washed his arms. The narrator expressed uncertainty concerning a wording that might imply repetition of washing the face.
He then wiped his forelock, wiped over his turban, and wiped over his leather socks.
We mounted and returned to the people after the prayer had already been established. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf had been put forward to lead them and had already completed one rakʿah and was in the second. We joined the row behind him, prayed the rakʿah we caught, and then completed the rakʿah we had missed.
Authentic: Narrated by Imām Aḥmad (18134).

ثم ذهب يحسر عن يديه وعليه جبة شامية ضيقة الكمين، فضاقت، فأخرج يديه من تحتها إخراجًا، فغسل وجهه ويديه — قال: فيجيء في الحديث غسل الوجه مرتين؟ قال: لا أدري ألكذا كان أم لا — ثم مسح بناصيته، ومسح على العمامة، ومسح على الخفين.
وركبنا فأدركنا القوم وقد أقيمت الصلاة، وقدموا عبد الرحمن بن عوف، وقد صلى بهم ركعة وهو في الثانية، فصففنا خلفه، فصلينا الركعة التي أدركنا، وقضينا الركعة التي سبقت.
صحيح: رواه الإمام أحمد (١٨١٣٤).
1591 — Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah was asked:
“Did anyone from this Ummah ever lead the Prophet ﷺ in prayer besides Abū Bakr may Allah be pleased with him?”
He replied: “Yes.”
We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey. In the latter part of the night, he struck the neck of my riding animal, and I thought that he had some need, so I turned aside with him. We continued until we were away from the people.
He dismounted and went off until he was hidden from my sight. He remained away for a long time, then returned and said:
“Do you have any need, O Mughīrah?”
I replied: “I have no need.”
He asked:
“Do you have water?”
I said: “Yes.”
I went to a waterskin—or another water container—hanging at the rear of the saddle and brought him water. I poured it for him, and he washed his hands thoroughly. The narrator said: “I am uncertain whether he said that he rubbed them with earth or not.”
He then washed his face. He tried to uncover his arms while wearing a Syrian cloak with tight sleeves, but the sleeves were too narrow, so he brought his arms out from beneath the cloak and washed his arms. The narrator expressed uncertainty concerning a wording that might imply repetition of washing the face.
He then wiped his forelock, wiped over his turban, and wiped over his leather socks.
We mounted and returned to the people after the prayer had already been established. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf had been put forward to lead them and had already completed one rakʿah and was in the second. We joined the row behind him, prayed the rakʿah we caught, and then completed the rakʿah we had missed.
Authentic: Narrated by Imām Aḥmad (18134).

«حاجتك يا مغيرة؟»

١٥٩٢ — عن أبي مالك الأشعري أنه جمع أصحابه فقال:
«هلمَّ أُصلي صلاة نبيكم ﷺ».
وكان رجلًا من الأشعريين.
قال: فدعا بجفنة من ماء، فغسل يديه ثلاثًا، ومضمض واستنشق، وغسل وجهه ثلاثًا، وذراعيه ثلاثًا، ومسح برأسه وأذنيه، وغسل قدميه.
قال: فصلى الظهر فقرأ فيها بفاتحة الكتاب، وكبر اثنتين وعشرين تكبيرة.
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٢٨٩٣)، والطبراني (٣٤١٢، ٣٤١٤)، وابن ماجه (٤١٧).

1592 — Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī gathered his companions and said:
“Come, and I will pray for you the prayer of your Prophet ﷺ.”
He was a man from the Ashʿarīs.
He called for a large bowl of water, washed his hands three times, rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose, washed his face three times, washed his forearms three times, wiped his head and ears, and washed his feet.
He then prayed Ẓuhr, recited Sūrat al-Fātiḥah in it, and pronounced twenty-two takbīrs.
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (22893), al-Ṭabarānī (3412, 3414), and Ibn Mājah (417).

١٥٩٦ — عن أبي جبير الكندي أنه قدم على رسول الله ﷺ، فأمر رسول الله ﷺ بوضوء وقال:
«توضأ يا أبا جبير».
فبدأ بفيه، فقال له رسول الله ﷺ:
«لا تبدأ بفيك، فإن الكافر يبدأ بفيه».
ثم دعا رسول الله ﷺ بوضوء، فغسل يديه حتى أنقاهما، ثم تمضمض واستنثر، ثم غسل وجهه ثلاثًا، ثم غسل يده اليمنى إلى المرفق ثلاثًا، ثم غسل يده اليسرى إلى المرفق ثلاثًا، ثم مسح برأسه وغسل رجليه.
حسن: رواه ابن حبان (١٠٨٩)، والبيهقي (١/٤٦).

1596 — Abū Jubayr al-Kindī reported that he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had water for wuḍūʾ brought and said:
“Perform wuḍūʾ, O Abū Jubayr.”
He began with his mouth, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Do not begin with your mouth, for the disbeliever begins with his mouth.”
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for water for wuḍūʾ. He washed his hands until they were thoroughly clean, rinsed his mouth and expelled water from his nose, washed his face three times, washed his right arm to the elbow three times, washed his left arm to the elbow three times, then wiped his head and washed his feet.

١٥٩٧ — عن النزال بن سبرة قال: رأيت عليًّا رضي الله عنه صلى الظهر، ثم قعد لحوائج الناس، فلما حضرت العصر أتي بتور من ماء، فأخذ منه كفًّا فمسح به وجهه وذراعيه ورأسه ورجليه، ثم أخذ فضله فشرب قائمًا، وقال:
إن الناس يكرهون هذا، وقد رأيت رسول الله ﷺ يفعله، وهذا وضوء من لم يحدث.
صحيح: رواه النسائي (١٣٠).

1597 — Al-Nazzāl ibn Sabrah said:
I saw ʿAlī may Allah be pleased with him pray Ẓuhr and then sit to attend to the needs of the people. When the time for ʿAṣr came, a basin of water was brought to him.
He took a handful of water and wiped his face, forearms, head, and feet. He then took the remaining water and drank it while standing.
He said:
“People dislike this, but I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do it. This is the wuḍūʾ of one who has not broken his wuḍūʾ.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (130).

١٥٩٨ — عن ابن عباس قال: توضأ رسول الله ﷺ فغرف غرفة، فمضمض واستنشق، ثم غرف غرفة فغسل وجهه، ثم غرف غرفة فغسل يده اليمنى، ثم غرف غرفة فغسل يده اليسرى، ثم مسح برأسه وأذنيه؛ باطنهما بالسبابتين، وظاهرهما بإبهاميه، ثم غرف غرفة فغسل رجله اليمنى، ثم غرف غرفة فغسل رجله اليسرى.
حسن: رواه النسائي (١٠٢)، واللفظ له، والترمذي (٣٦)، وابن ماجه (٤٣٩)، وابن خزيمة (١٤٨)، وابن حبان (١٠٧٨).
ولفظ الترمذي:
«مسح رسول الله ﷺ برأسه وأذنيه ظاهرهما وباطنهما».
ولفظ ابن ماجه:
«أن رسول الله ﷺ مسح أذنيه داخلهما بالسبابتين، وخالف إبهاميه إلى ظاهر أذنيه، فمسح ظاهرهما وباطنهما».

english_source:
1598 — Ibn ʿAbbās said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed wuḍūʾ. He scooped one handful of water and rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose. He then scooped another handful and washed his face, another handful and washed his right arm, and another handful and washed his left arm.
He then wiped his head and ears, wiping the inner parts of the ears with his index fingers and their outer parts with his thumbs.
He then scooped another handful and washed his right foot, and another handful and washed his left foot.
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (102), whose wording this is, al-Tirmidhī (36), Ibn Mājah (439), Ibn Khuzaymah (148), and Ibn Ḥibbān (1078).
Al-Tirmidhī’s wording is:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiped his head and his ears, their outer and inner parts.”
Ibn Mājah’s wording is:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiped the inner parts of his ears with his index fingers, moved his thumbs to the outer parts of his ears, and wiped both their outer and inner parts.”

١٦٠٢ — عن عاصم بن لقيط بن صبرة، عن أبيه قال: كنت وافد بني المنتفق، أو في وفد بني المنتفق إلى رسول الله ﷺ، فذكر قصة نزوله على عائشة، وأنها أمرت بصنع خزيرة إلى أن لقي رسول الله ﷺ، فقال:
يا رسول الله، أخبرني عن الوضوء.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ:
«أسبغ الوضوء، وخلل بين الأصابع، وبالغ في الاستنشاق إلا أن تكون صائمًا».
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (١٤٢)، واللفظ له، والترمذي (٣٨)، والنسائي (١١٤)، وابن ماجه (٤٠٧، ٤٤٨).
وفي بعض الروايات:
«إذا توضأت فمضمض».
وقال الترمذي: «حسن صحيح».
والخزيرة: لحم يقطع صغارًا، ويصب عليه ماء كثير، فإذا نضج ذر عليه الدقيق.

english_source:
1602 — ʿĀṣim ibn Laqīṭ ibn Ṣabrah reported from his father, who said:
I was the representative of Banū al-Muntafiq, or among the delegation of Banū al-Muntafiq. He then mentioned the account of his staying with ʿĀʾishah and her ordering that khazīrah be prepared.
He then said:
“O Messenger of Allah, tell me about wuḍūʾ.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Perform wuḍūʾ thoroughly, wash between the fingers, and be thorough in drawing water into the nose, except when you are fasting.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (142), whose wording this is, al-Tirmidhī (38), al-Nasāʾī (114), and Ibn Mājah (407, 448).
In some narrations:
“When you perform wuḍūʾ, rinse your mouth.”
Al-Tirmidhī said: “Ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.”
Khazīrah is meat cut into small pieces over which plenty of water is poured; when it is cooked, flour is sprinkled into it.

١٦٠٣ — عن المستورد بن شداد قال: رأيت رسول الله ﷺ إذا توضأ يدلك أصابع رجليه بخنصره.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٤٨)، والترمذي (٤٠)، وابن ماجه (٤٤٦). وقال الترمذي: «هذا حديث حسن غريب».

english_source:
1603 — Al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddād said:
I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when performing wuḍūʾ, rub between the toes of his feet with his little finger.
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (148), al-Tirmidhī (40), and Ibn Mājah (446). Al-Tirmidhī said: “This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.”

١٦٠٤ — عن عبد الله بن عباس أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«إذا توضأت فخلل بين أصابع يديك ورجليك».
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٣٩)، وابن ماجه (٤٤٧)، واللفظ للترمذي.
ولفظ ابن ماجه:
«إذا قمت إلى الصلاة فأسبغ الوضوء، واجعل الماء بين أصابع يديك ورجليك».
قال الترمذي: حسن غريب.

english_source:
1604 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When you perform wuḍūʾ, wash between the fingers of your hands and the toes of your feet.”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (39) and Ibn Mājah (447). This wording is that of al-Tirmidhī.
Ibn Mājah’s wording is:
“When you stand for prayer, perform wuḍūʾ thoroughly and cause the water to reach between the fingers of your hands and the toes of your feet.”
Al-Tirmidhī said: “Ḥasan gharīb.”

1606 — Abū Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When one of you awakens from sleep and performs wuḍūʾ, let him expel water from his nose three times, for Satan spends the night upon his nostrils.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3295) and Muslim (238).

“When one of you awakens from sleep and performs wuḍūʾ, let him expel water from his nose three times, for Satan spends the night upon his nostrils.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3295) and Muslim (238).

١٦٠٨ — عن عبد الله بن مغفل أنه سمع ابنه يقول:
اللهم إني أسألك القصر الأبيض عن يمين الجنة إذا دخلتها.
فقال:
أي بني، سل الله الجنة، وتعوذ به من النار؛ فإني سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«إنه سيكون في هذه الأمة قوم يعتدون في الطهور والدعاء».
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٩٦)، وابن ماجه (٣٨٦٤)، إلا أن ابن ماجه لم يذكر «الطهور».

1608 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Mughaffal heard his son saying:
“O Allah, I ask You for the white palace on the right side of Paradise when I enter it.”
He said:
“My son, ask Allah for Paradise and seek refuge in Him from the Fire, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
‘There will be people in this Ummah who transgress the proper limits in purification and supplication.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (96) and Ibn Mājah (3864), except that Ibn Mājah’s narration does not mention “purification.”

١٦٠٩ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده قال: جاء أعرابي إلى النبي ﷺ فسأله عن الوضوء، فأراه ثلاثًا ثلاثًا، ثم قال:
«هَذَا الْوُضُوءُ، فَمَنْ زَادَ عَلَى هَذَا فَقَدْ أَسَاءَ، أَوْ تَعَدَّى، أَوْ ظَلَمَ».
حسن: رواه ابن ماجه (٤٢٢)، واللفظ له، وأبو داود (١٣٥)، والنسائي (١/٨٨)، وأحمد (٢٦٨٤)، وابن خزيمة (١٧٤).

english_source:
1609 — ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that a Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about wuḍūʾ. He showed him wuḍūʾ, washing each part three times, then said:
“This is wuḍūʾ. Whoever goes beyond this has acted badly, exceeded the proper limit, or acted unjustly.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (422), whose wording this is, Abū Dāwūd (135), al-Nasāʾī (1/88), Aḥmad (2684), and Ibn Khuzaymah (174).

١٦١٠ — عن ابن عباس قال: بِتُّ عند خالتي ميمونة، فقام النبي ﷺ فتوضأ من شَنَّةٍ وضوءًا يُقَلِّلُه، فقمت فصنعت كما صنع.
صحيح: رواه ابن ماجه (٤٢٤)، واللفظ له، وابن خزيمة (١٥٣٣).
وقوله: «شَنَّة»؛ أي: قِربة.
وقوله: «يُقَلِّلُه»؛ أي: لا يكثر من استعمال الماء. وفي رواية: «توضأ وضوءًا خفيفًا»، والمعنى واحد.

english_source:
1610 — Ibn ʿAbbās said: I spent the night at the house of my maternal aunt Maymūnah. The Prophet ﷺ got up and performed wuḍūʾ from a shannah, a water-skin, using only a small amount of water. I then got up and did as he had done.
Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (424), whose wording this is, and Ibn Khuzaymah (1533).
A shannah is a water-skin.
The expression “using only a small amount” means that he did not use an excessive quantity of water. In another narration: “He performed a light wuḍūʾ,” and the meaning is the same.

١٦١١ — عن أبي هريرة قال: أسبغوا الوضوء؛ فإن أبا القاسم ﷺ قال:
«وَيْلٌ لِلْأَعْقَابِ مِنَ النَّارِ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٦٥)، واللفظ له، ومسلم (٢٤٢).
وفي مسلم أن رسول الله ﷺ رأى رجلًا لم يغسل عقبيه فقال:
«وَيْلٌ لِلْأَعْقَابِ مِنَ النَّارِ».

1611 — Abū Hurayrah said:
“Perform wuḍūʾ thoroughly, for Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ said:
‘Woe to the heels from the Fire.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (165), whose wording this is, and Muslim (242).
In Muslim’s narration, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a man who had not washed his heels and said:
“Woe to the heels from the Fire.”

١٦١٢ — عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: أخبرني عمر بن الخطاب أن رجلًا توضأ فترك موضع ظفر على قدمه، فأبصره النبي ﷺ فقال:
«ارْجِعْ فَأَحْسِنْ وُضُوءَكَ».
فرجع ثم صلى.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤٣).

1612 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb informed me that a man performed wuḍūʾ but left an area on his foot the size of a fingernail dry. The Prophet ﷺ saw it and said:
“Go back and perform your wuḍūʾ properly.”
So he returned, then prayed.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (243).

١٦١٤ — عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص قال: تخلف النبي ﷺ عنا في سفرة سافرناها، فأدركنا وقد أرهقنا العصر، فجعلنا نتوضأ ونمسح على أرجلنا، فنادى بأعلى صوته:
«وَيْلٌ لِلْأَعْقَابِ مِنَ النَّارِ».
مرتين أو ثلاثًا.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٦٣)، واللفظ له، ومسلم (٢٤١).
وفي رواية قال: رجعنا مع رسول الله ﷺ من مكة إلى المدينة، حتى إذا كنا بماء بالطريق تعجل قوم عند العصر، فتوضؤوا وهم عجال، فانتهينا إليهم وأعقابهم تلوح لم يمسها الماء، فقال رسول الله ﷺ:
«وَيْلٌ لِلْأَعْقَابِ مِنَ النَّارِ، أَسْبِغُوا الْوُضُوءَ».

1614 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: The Prophet ﷺ remained behind us during a journey. He caught up with us when the time for ʿAṣr had become pressing. We began performing wuḍūʾ and were merely passing water over our feet, so he called out at the top of his voice:
“Woe to the heels from the Fire!”
He repeated it two or three times.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (163), whose wording this is, and Muslim (241).
In another narration, he said:
We returned with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Makkah to Madinah. When we reached some water along the road, a group hurried because of ʿAṣr and performed wuḍūʾ hastily. We came upon them while their heels were visibly dry and had not been touched by water. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Woe to the heels from the Fire. Perform wuḍūʾ thoroughly.”

١٦١٧ — عن عبد الله بن عباس قال: والله ما خصنا رسول الله ﷺ بشيء دون الناس إلا ثلاثة أشياء؛ فإنه أمرنا أن نُسبغ الوضوء، ولا نأكل الصدقة، ولا نُنزي الحُمُر على الخيل.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٨٠٨)، والنسائي (١٤١)، والترمذي (١٧١٠)، واللفظ لهما، وابن ماجه (٤٢٦). وقال الترمذي: حسن صحيح.

1617 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās said:
“By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not single us out with anything apart from the rest of the people except three things: he commanded us to perform wuḍūʾ thoroughly, not to consume charity, and not to breed donkeys with horses.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (808), al-Nasāʾī (141), al-Tirmidhī (1710), whose wording is followed, and Ibn Mājah (426). Al-Tirmidhī said: Ḥasan Ṣaḥīḥ.

arabic_source:
١٦٢١ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
«أَلَا أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى مَا يَمْحُو اللهُ بِهِ الْخَطَايَا، وَيَرْفَعُ بِهِ الدَّرَجَاتِ؟»
قالوا: بلى يا رسول الله.
قال:
«إِسْبَاغُ الْوُضُوءِ عَلَى الْمَكَارِهِ، وَكَثْرَةُ الْخُطَا إِلَى الْمَسَاجِدِ، وَانْتِظَارُ الصَّلَاةِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ، فَذَلِكُمُ الرِّبَاطُ».
وفي رواية:
«فَذَلِكُمُ الرِّبَاطُ، فَذَلِكُمُ الرِّبَاطُ».
صحيح: رواه مالك (٥٥)، ومسلم (٢٥١). وفي لفظ مالك كرر: «ذلكم الرباط» ثلاث مرات.
وقوله: «المكاره» جمع مَكْرَه، وهو ما يكرهه الإنسان ويشق عليه. والكُرْه، بالضم والفتح، المشقة. والمعنى أن يتوضأ مع البرد الشديد، والعلل التي يتأذى معها بمس الماء.
وقوله: «ذلكم الرباط»؛ أي: الرباط المرغب فيه. وأصل الرباط الحبس على الشيء، فكأنه حبس نفسه على هذه الطاعة.

1621 — Abū Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Shall I not direct you to that by which Allah erases sins and raises ranks?”
They replied:
“Yes, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“Performing wuḍūʾ thoroughly despite hardship, taking many steps to the mosques, and waiting for one prayer after another. That is ribāṭ.”
In another narration:
“That is ribāṭ; that is ribāṭ.”
Authentic: Narrated by Mālik (55) and Muslim (251). In Mālik’s wording, “That is ribāṭ” is repeated three times.
The word “hardships” refers to things that a person dislikes or finds difficult. The meaning includes performing wuḍūʾ despite severe cold or physical conditions in which contact with water causes discomfort.
The statement “That is ribāṭ” means the ribāṭ for which encouragement and reward are promised. The basic meaning of ribāṭ is remaining bound or steadfast upon something; it is as though the person restrains himself upon this act of obedience.

«أَلَا أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى مَا يُكَفِّرُ اللهُ بِهِ الْخَطَايَا، وَيَزِيدُ بِهِ فِي الْحَسَنَاتِ؟»
قالوا: بلى يا رسول الله.
قال:

english_source:
1623 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reported that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Shall I not tell you what Allah uses to expiate sins and increase good deeds?”
They replied:
“Yes, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“Performing wuḍūʾ thoroughly despite hardship, taking many steps to the mosques, and waiting for one prayer after another.”
In another narration, with an additional passage:
“No man among you leaves his home in a state of purification, prays the prayer with the Muslims, and then remains seated waiting for the next prayer, except that the angels say: ‘O Allah, forgive him. O Allah, have mercy upon him.’
When you stand for prayer, straighten your rows, establish them properly, and close the gaps, for I see you from behind my back.
When your imam says, ‘Allāhu akbar,’ then say, ‘Allāhu akbar.’ When he bows, then bow. And when he says, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him,’ then say, ‘O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs all praise.’
The best rows of the men are the front rows and the worst are the rear rows; and the best rows of the women are the rear rows and the worst are the front rows.
O assembly of women, when the men prostrate, lower your gazes so that you do not see the private parts of the men because of the tightness of their waist-wrappers.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (427) and Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah (1/7). The second, longer narration is narrated by Aḥmad (10994).

١٦٢٤ — عن أنس قال: كان النبي ﷺ يتوضأ عند كل صلاة.
قال عمرو بن عامر: فكيف كنتم تصنعون؟
قال: كان يجزئ أحدنا الوضوء ما لم يُحدث.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢١٤).
وعند الترمذي (٥٨):
«كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ يَتَوَضَّأُ لِكُلِّ صَلَاةٍ طَاهِرًا أَوْ غَيْرَ طَاهِرٍ».

1624 — Anas said:
“The Prophet ﷺ used to perform wuḍūʾ for every prayer.”
ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir asked:
“What did you yourselves use to do?”
He replied:
“One wuḍūʾ was sufficient for one of us so long as he had not broken it.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (214).
In al-Tirmidhī (58):
“The Prophet ﷺ used to perform wuḍūʾ for every prayer, whether he was already in a state of purity or not.”

«كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ يَتَوَضَّأُ لِكُلِّ صَلَاةٍ طَاهِرًا أَوْ غَيْرَ طَاهِرٍ».
1624 — Anas said:
“The Prophet ﷺ used to perform wuḍūʾ for every prayer.”
ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir asked:
“What did you yourselves use to do?”
He replied:
“One wuḍūʾ was sufficient for one of us so long as he had not broken it.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (214).
In al-Tirmidhī (58):
“The Prophet ﷺ used to perform wuḍūʾ for every prayer, whether he was already in a state of purity or not.”

١٦٢٥ — عن سويد بن النعمان قال: خرجنا مع رسول الله ﷺ عام خيبر، حتى إذا كنا بالصهباء صلى لنا رسول الله ﷺ العصر، فلما صلى دعا بالأطعمة، فلم يؤت إلا بالسويق، فأكلنا وشربنا، ثم قام النبي ﷺ إلى المغرب، فمضمض، ثم صلى المغرب ولم يتوضأ.

١٦٢٦ — عن بريدة أن النبي ﷺ صلى الصلوات يوم الفتح بوضوء واحد، ومسح على خفيه، فقال له عمر:
لقد صنعت اليوم شيئًا لم تكن تصنعه!
قال:
«عَمْدًا صَنَعْتُهُ يَا عُمَرُ».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٧٧).
وعند الترمذي (٦١): كان النبي ﷺ يتوضأ لكل صلاة، فلما كان يوم الفتح صلى الصلوات كلها بوضوء واحد.
وفي الباب ترك الوضوء مما مسته النار: حديث جابر أن النبي ﷺ ذُبح له شاة فأكل، ثم قام إلى صلاة الظهر، ثم أُتي ببقية الشاة، وحضرت الصلاة فقام وصلى ولم يمس ماءً؛ فجمع بين الصلاتين بوضوء واحد، كل منهما في وقتها.
